aesthetic: Codex Marginalia — a typographic system modelled on the illuminated manuscript page, where cream fields, ink accents, and ruled left-margins create the book as interface
chromaticArc: Opens on vellum cream (slides 1–4), drops to ink-dark for the first section divider (slide 5), resurfaces through warm parchment for the development run (slides 6–9), pauses on antique-gold mid-tone (slide 10), returns to cream through the closing arc (slides 11–13), drops again to ink for the penultimate divider (slide 14), and resolves on vellum cream — four light/dark crossings across fifteen pages.
gridStrategy: Every title anchors at col 6 with span varying between 22 and 36 to shift gravitational weight; body text migrates vertically between row 18 and row 26 while never exceeding span 36, preserving col 42–60 as structural silence — compositional variety comes from title span width, row drop, and occasional body offset to col 10, not from abandoning the left-margin discipline.

fontStrategy.secondarySlides: Georgia appears on slides 7 and 12 — aphorism or pull-quote slides where a single large italic phrase at weight 400 and generous tracking occupies most of the field, exploiting Georgia's compressed letterforms for maximum editorial warmth

accentStrategy: A thin vertical rule (type: line, col 5, rowSpan full) anchors the left gutter as a running chapter margin on roughly 45% of slides; on the two ink-dark section dividers this rule is replaced by a 3-column antique-gold bar at col 6 acting as a folio marker, and on five light slides a short horizontal rule at row 14 separates title zone from body zone with calligraphic restraint.
